problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a collection of archival boxes onto a fleet of uniform pallets for secure transport. The archival boxes are as follows:

* Document Set Alpha: 66 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Beta: 31 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Gamma: 45 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Delta: 67 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Epsilon: 30 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Zeta: 53 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Eta: 53 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Theta: 51 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Iota: 35 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Kappa: 66 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Lambda: 53 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Mu: 53 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Nu: 34 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Xi: 56 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Omicron: 42 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Pi: 53 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Rho: 66 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Sigma: 46 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Tau: 39 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Upsilon: 43 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Phi: 63 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Chi: 41 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Psi: 68 cubic decimeters
* Document Set Omega: 38 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Y: 62 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Z: 37 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Left Bracket: 50 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Backslash: 67 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Right Bracket: 67 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Caret: 65 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Underscore: 70 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle Grave: 69 cubic decimeters
* Archive Bundle a: 36 cubic decimeters

Each pallet is certified to support a maximum volumetric load of 100 cubic decimeters. The coordinator must assign every archival box to precisely one pallet, ensuring the cumulative volume on any pallet does not surpass its certified limit, while utilizing the smallest possible number of pallets for the entire consignment.
